description: The plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for several variants of large language models, including a baseline “Vanilla” model and multiple configurations of the proposed “SepLLM” and “StrmLLM” methods. The x-axis, labeled “#Iteration,” spans from 0 to 140,000 with linear spacing and tick marks every 20,000 iterations. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” ranges from 2.4 to 3.4 with linear scaling and tick marks at intervals of 0.1. The “Vanilla” model (purple line with circle markers) starts at approximately 3.35 loss and steadily declines to around 2.5 by 140,000 iterations. “StrmLLM (n=64)” (blue line with square markers) begins near 3.35 and decreases to about 2.62. “SepLLM (n=64)” (orange line with diamond markers) starts slightly lower than StrmLLM and converges to approximately 2.55. “SepLLM (n=64, H)” (green line with triangle markers) follows a similar trajectory to the standard SepLLM but ends slightly higher, around 2.57. “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” (red line with inverted triangle markers) begins near 3.3 and converges to about 2.53. “SepLLM (n=128)” (dark blue line with pentagon markers) starts at 3.35 and converges to approximately 2.52, showing a slightly steeper initial drop than the n=64 variants. All models exhibit a rapid initial decline in loss followed by a slower convergence toward their final values.
